items.title: Configs & setup for a new collaborator or LLM
items.why: This project needs local CLI tools, Roblox Studio, Rojo, MCP connections, and GitHub access before an agent can safely edit, test, or push the game.
items.blocks: Reliable Rojo sync, live Studio compatibility tests, Blender work, and GitHub delivery
items.when: Before the first implementation or compatibility run on a new machine.
steps: Install Python 3, Git, Roblox Studio, and Homebrew (macOS). Install the project CLIs: `brew install rojo stylua selene lune gh uv`.
From the repository root, verify the tools: `rojo --version`, `stylua --version`, `selene --version`, `lune --version`, `gh --version`, and `python3 --version`.

Configure Codex MCP servers: `codex mcp add Roblox_Studio -- /Applications/RobloxStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/StudioMCP` and `codex mcp add blender -- uvx blender-mcp`; restart Codex and verify with `codex mcp list`. On another OS, use that StudioMCP executable path.

For Blender live editing, install the add-on with `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon`, enable it in Blender, and start the BlenderMCP server from the N-panel. Headless exports do not need the live connection.
Start Rojo from the repository root with `rojo serve`; in Roblox Studio open Plugins > Rojo and connect to `localhost:34872`. Confirm the synced script matches the files on disk before testing.

Open the Roblox Studio place in Edit mode, enable the Roblox Studio MCP, and turn on Game Settings > Security > Enable Studio Access to API Services when real DataStore tests are needed. Set the place server size to 7 for the workshop.
Authenticate GitHub for branch and push workflows: `gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web`; verify with `gh auth status`.
Start the shared dashboard with `python3 tools/dashboard/server.py --no-fetch --no-auto-branch` and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. Use the dashboard Agents tab and manual tasks as the handoff record.

Run local checks before a live gate: `stylua --check src`, `selene src`, and `rojo build --output /tmp/racer-rng.rbxl`. Never run two Studio test sessions at once, never edit synced scripts inside Studio, and do not push without an ALL GREEN `/compat-check`.

items.title: Save the place after the stray spawn was deleted
items.why: Claude deleted the stray Workspace.SpawnLocation (-2, 0.5, -2) in Edit mode. Studio only keeps that change if you save; otherwise it comes back next time and the spawn_area test fails again.
items.blocks: Keeping spawn_area green (exactly one spawn in the game)
items.when: After the compat check finishes (play stopped), not during a test run.
steps: Make sure play is stopped (Edit mode).
Check Explorer: Workspace has no `SpawnLocation` directly under it (Workspace.SpawnArea is built only during play).
Press Ctrl+S (File > Save to Roblox) to save the place.
Mark this done.
items.verified: Claude, 2026-10-05: after a Studio restart the place has exactly one SpawnLocation (SpawnArea.Spawn) during play.

items.title: Remove the extra Baseplate saved in the place
items.why: world-tester found two identical Workspace.Baseplate parts (2048x16x2048 at 0,-8,0), both purple-ish (180,107,191) instead of the green Rojo defines in default.project.json. One is most likely an old Baseplate saved in the place file next to the Rojo one. Harmless for physics, but it z-fights and hides the intended green ground.
items.blocks: Nothing (cosmetic, keeps the place matching the repo)
items.when: With the place save after the compat check (Studio in Edit mode).
steps: In Edit mode, select Workspace and look for two children named `Baseplate`.
Decide which ground colour you want: green (the repo's default.project.json) or purple. If purple is intended, tell Claude so it updates default.project.json instead.
Delete the one that is NOT managed by Rojo (Rojo recreates its own on sync; if unsure, delete one, wait a few seconds and check one Baseplate remains).
Save the place (Ctrl+S).

items.title: Reopen Studio so the compat check can finish
items.why: The compat check stopped halfway: the harness ran (23/24 pass) but the UI, multiplayer and world testers were cut off by a usage limit, and Studio is no longer connected to Claude.
items.blocks: An ALL GREEN /compat-check, which is what lets initial-import go to main
items.when: Now.
steps: Open Roblox Studio with the place "Racer RNG" (Edit mode, not playing).
Make sure the Roblox Studio MCP is enabled (Assistant settings) and the Rojo plugin is connected (`rojo serve` is already running in the project).

Optional but recommended: in the Explorer, delete `Workspace.SpawnLocation` (the default spawn at -2, 0.5, -2; NOT `Workspace.SpawnArea.Spawn`) and save the place (Ctrl+S). It is the only harness failure: the game must have exactly one spawn. If you skip this, Claude deletes it in Edit mode and asks you to save.
Tell Claude "Studio is open".

Pick `~/Documents/RobloxGames/blender/exports/rusty_hatchback/RustyHatchback.fbx`.
In the importer check the size reads about 6.6 studs long. If it is 100x too big or small, change the file units (Stud / Meter) until it does.

items.why: Under device emulation (e.g. 750x361 phone) Studio's injected mouse clicks land at the wrong screen point, so the UI suite's ~57 click contracts can't run. Automation can't change the setting during Play (the menu is greyed out).

items.title: Play one duel with two clients in Studio
items.why: The duel request is a ProximityPrompt on another player's avatar. The Studio MCP starts one client only, so Claude cannot walk up to a second player. The server flow is covered by the `duel` harness scenario with fake players and the UI by `ui_duel`; the real prompt, the real seats and the countdown on two screens are not.
items.blocks: Calling the duel feature verified end to end (docs/DUEL_SPEC.md section 4, multiplayer flow)
items.when: When no agent session is using Studio.
steps: Studio > Test tab > Clients and Servers: pick `Local Server`, `2 Players`, press Start. Rojo must be connected first.
In client 1 check: no `Duel` prompt on your own avatar.
Walk client 1 next to client 2's avatar (within 10 studs). A `Duel` prompt with the other player's name shows; hold F.
Client 1: the PICK A TRACK panel opens; click `TRACK 1`.
Client 2: the DUEL REQUEST panel shows `<name> challenges you on Track 1`; click ACCEPT.
Both: a car each at the Track 1 start, side by side, `3 2 1 GO!`, both cars race to the finish. During the countdown press R and W: the car must not move.
Both: `YOU WIN!` on one screen and `YOU LOSE` on the other, then both stand in the spawn area. Money is unchanged.
Repeat once with DECLINE (client 1 sees `DUEL DECLINED`) and once pressing STOP AUTO mid-race (the other player wins).
Tell Claude what happened at each step.

items.title: Enable Mesh / Image APIs for the published game
items.why: Biome props build their CC0 meshes on each client with EditableMesh, which fails by default in published games; without the toggle players only see the plain-part fallbacks.

steps: Open the game in Studio: File > Game Settings (or Home > Game Settings).
Security: turn on "Allow Mesh / Image APIs" (review the linked Terms of Use first). The same toggle is in the Creator Dashboard: the experience > Configure > Settings.
Save.
Tell Claude "mesh APIs on"; Claude checks a live server shows meshes.
items.note: Owner confirmed 2026-10-20: Allow Mesh / Image APIs was already on. Live-server mesh check happens after the biome branch is merged and published.

items.title: Open Cloud API key for the car mesh uploads
items.why: The redesigned cars are Blender MeshParts (docs/CAR_REDESIGN_SPEC.md). Each car's FBX has to be uploaded to Roblox to get mesh ids; doing 111 by hand in Studio's 3D Importer is very slow.
items.blocks: car-redesign: every wave (the Go-Kart pilot FBX is ready in drafts/cars/go_kart/redesign/)
items.when: Before wave 1
steps: Open create.roblox.com > Dashboard > Open Cloud > API Keys > Create API Key.
Name it "car-redesign-upload". Add the API system "Assets" with Read and Write. Under Accepted IP Addresses add 0.0.0.0/0 (or your IP).
Save, copy the key and keep it private. Do not paste it in chat or commit it.
In a terminal: echo 'export ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_KEY=<key>' >> ~/.zshrc and echo 'export ROBLOX_CREATOR_ID=<your user id or group id>' >> ~/.zshrc, then open a new terminal.
Tell Claude "upload key set"; Claude pilots the Go-Kart upload. If Open Cloud does not work, the fallback is importing each FBX with Studio's 3D Importer.
items.note: Verified 2026-10-20: Go-Kart pilot uploaded (Model 90296948247442) with /usr/bin/python3 (python.org 3.14 lacks CA certs).

items.title: Re-bake the Racer UI ScreenGuis into StarterGui.rbxm

RacerIndex, RacerStats, RacerSettings, RacerRebirth and RacerUpgrades now carry a newer SpecHash than the baked assets/studio/StarterGui.rbxm, so Bind rebuilds them from code at runtime instead of using the saved GUIs. Done 2026-10-26 by Claude offline with Lune (no Studio save needed): RacerStats, RacerSettings, RacerRebirth, RacerUpgrades and RollShowcase re-baked; all seven baked SpecHashes match their modules; verify.py --lune passes; live Play shows no client errors.
items.blocks: Nothing breaks (Bind falls back to Build); the baked asset just stops being used for those five GUIs until refreshed.
steps: Open the place in Studio with `rojo serve` running and Rojo connected (Edit mode, not Play).

For each of RacerIndex, RacerStats, RacerSettings, RacerRebirth and RacerUpgrades, run ui/generated/<Name>.studio.luau in the command bar (no studio.luau for Stats/Settings: ask Claude to generate one) so StarterGui holds the new ScreenGui.

Say what to change (shape, colours, wings, effects strength), or approve.
On approval: decide when the effects play (always, or only on boost) so the design doc can record it.

items.title: Reconnect Rojo in Studio and save the place
items.why: Studio was restarted, so its Rojo plugin is disconnected. The Ember Wyvern was built into ReplicatedStorage.RedesignCarModels by hand; Rojo replaces it with assets/studio/RedesignCarModels/ember_wyvern.rbxmx once connected.
items.blocks: Studio matching the files on disk (every later test run).
steps: Keep `rojo serve` running in the project root (it is).
In Studio: Plugins > Rojo > Connect.
Check ReplicatedStorage.RedesignCarModels.ember_wyvern has 7 MeshParts, then File > Save.
items.note: Verified: Studio scripts match disk (RedesignTests synced live); RedesignCarModels.ember_wyvern present once.

items.title: Save the Studio place (rigged Ember Wyvern model)
items.why: Rojo cannot create or update MeshParts (MeshId is plugin-locked), so ReplicatedStorage.RedesignCarModels.ember_wyvern (rigged, 33 bones, Model 100205140229978 (long tail)) was built in Studio through MCP. It only persists when the place is saved; assets/studio/RedesignCarModels/ember_wyvern.rbxmx on disk is the same model for rojo build.
items.blocks: The flying wyvern in a published game and in the next Studio session.
steps: In Studio (edit mode) check ReplicatedStorage.RedesignCarModels.ember_wyvern: Body has a Root bone tree, the model has attribute Rig = Wyvern.
File > Save (or Publish to Roblox when you ship).
